title: Valid Palindrome
kidExplanation: Ignore spaces and punctuation. Do the letters and digits read the same forwards and backwards?
plainProblem: Valid Palindrome: Ignore spaces and punctuation. Worked example — input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"; expected output: true. Why: Alphanumeric palindrome. Interview pattern to name out loud: Two pointers from both ends (or slow/fast).

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

thinkingSteps.body: For “Valid Palindrome”, first say a correct slow approach: scan or retry every candidate until the example works by hand. Input s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama" should still produce true.

thinkingSteps.title: Why it is slow
thinkingSteps.body: Count the nested work. If each choice restarts a full scan, time blows up. Name the cost before optimizing — interviewers want that honesty. Target after the insight: O(n).

thinkingSteps.title: Aha insight
thinkingSteps.body: To determine if a given string is a valid palindrome, we can use two pointers approach. We initialize two pointers, one at the beginning of the string (left) and the other at the end of the string (right). We then compare characters at these two pointers. If they are both alphanumeric characters and equal in value (ignoring case), we move both pointers towards the center of the string. If they are not equal, we know the string is not a palindrome. We continue this process until the two pointers meet or cross each other.
